title: Several owned things: Nämä ovat …
focus: Drop plural -t before the owner ending; use Nämä ovat for several things.
targetSkills: Plural possessed nouns in ownership sentences

exercises.prompt: Complete “These are my games.” Nämä ovat minun ___. Use peli (“game”), pelit (“games”), and -ni.
exercises.explanation: Remove plural -t before the owner ending: pelit + -ni gives pelini. Nämä ovat still shows several things.
requiredSkills: Plural possessed nouns in ownership sentences
exercises.targetSkill: Plural possessed nouns in ownership sentences
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Plural possessed nouns in ownership sentences: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.pattern: demonstrative + agreeing olla + optional owner pronoun + possessed noun

parts.formation: Nämä is the plural of tämä: several things.
Use ovat with several things, independently of how many people own them.
Minun is the personal owner form of minä; it selects -ni.
pelit (“games”) loses its plural -t before -ni: peli + -ni = pelini.

optionFeedback.pelitni: The plural -t disappears before a possessive suffix; use pelini.
optionFeedback.pelit: This personal owner phrase needs its supplied ending -ni; use pelini.
optionFeedback.pelisi: Keep the supplied ending -ni for minun; use pelini.

exercises.prompt: Repair “Nämä ovat minun talotni.” to mean “These are my houses.” Keep minun; use talo (“house”), talot (“houses”), and -ni.
exercises.explanation: Nämä ovat identifies several things. The ending -ni identifies my ownership.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: demonstrative + agreeing olla + optional owner pronoun + possessed noun

parts.formation: Nämä is the plural of tämä: several things.
Use ovat with several things, independently of how many people own them.
Minun is the personal owner form of minä; it selects -ni.
talot (“houses”) loses its plural -t before -ni: talo + -ni = taloni.

answerDiagnostics.explanation: Drop the noun’s plural -t before -ni: use taloni.
Keep the possessive ending -ni even when the owner pronoun is present or omitted.
Minun needs -ni; changing the ending changes the owner.
These are several things: Nämä needs ovat, regardless of the number of owners.
